title: Roll out a pricing change
summary: Change prices without burning the base: model the revenue impact, decide who gets grandfathered, create the new plans, migrate subscriptions, announce it honestly, and watch churn and MRR through the transition.

parts.title: Model the revenue impact of the new pricing
parts.guidance: Compare current and proposed pricing against actual customer quantities, discounts, usage and renewal patterns. Show representative invoices and scenarios for customer responses, keeping recurring revenue definitions and currencies consistent. Separate modeled revenue uplift from cash collection. Give the pricing decision-maker the assumptions and sensitivities that materially change the result, especially for customers facing the largest increases.

parts.title: Decide grandfathering and migration policy
parts.guidance: Group customers into retained terms, new pricing and cases needing individual review. Check contracts and commitments with the commercial and legal reviewers for relevant notice, acceptance and renewal conditions. Define effective dates, discount treatment and exception authority. Produce a customer-level migration policy, keeping unresolved accounts out of the change batch until their obligations and treatment are established.

parts.title: Create the new plans in billing
parts.guidance: Create the new plans from the pricing matrix in a draft or test catalog, preserving identifiers still used by current subscriptions. Check currency, interval, unit, usage limits and customer wording through checkout and invoice previews. Map each old plan to its intended successor and specify which remain available. Release the new catalog within billing authority; moving subscriptions requires the separate migration policy.

parts.title: Migrate or grandfather existing subscriptions
parts.guidance: Build the exact subscription batch from the migration policy, excluding grandfathered and unresolved accounts. Preview effective dates, billing periods, discounts, credits and immediate charges with the provider's supported tools. Confirm required notices or acceptance and billing authority for that batch. Apply and reconcile each account; inspect partial failures before retrying so a customer is not charged twice or moved outside the policy.

references.title: Change the price of existing subscriptions

parts.title: Update the site pricing page and docs
parts.guidance: Use the billing pricing matrix to update the public pricing page, plan comparisons and help material. Explain units, intervals, limits and treatment of existing customers consistently. In preview, follow each purchase link to the intended plan and price. Publish the pricing owner's agreed version, then compare live amounts, destinations and support guidance with the released catalog.

parts.title: Announce the change to customers
parts.guidance: Write each customer notice for that recipient's actual transition group: old and new terms, effective date, required action and support contact. Follow the contract and jurisdiction review for notice or acceptance requirements. Send the commercial owner's agreed messages to the mapped recipients on the required schedule. Track responses and return disputed or unresolved accounts to the migration owner before their billing change.

parts.title: Monitor churn and MRR through the transition
parts.guidance: Compare affected cohorts with the pre-change baseline for recurring revenue, cancellations, downgrades and expansion. Reconcile planned transitions with actual invoices and charges to distinguish implementation errors from customer decisions. Read support complaints alongside the numbers. Report the window, cohort sizes and data gaps, and identify concrete corrections where billing behavior or customer understanding differs from the policy.

metadata.supportReason: Plan modeling, the billing migration, and the comms are automatable over billing and email APIs; the grandfathering call is a judgment the founder owns.
